sentences.text: Namaskar.
Sutra 11 has to be approached from the perspective of a Siddha or Jivamukta,
and in the light of his or her integral experience and mode of activity.
The meaning hangs on the translation of Charya,
which in the context of the Agamas denotes the practice and conduct of an initiate,
but here is not related to any rules of behavior, but to a state transcending them.
The number five is all-inclusive, but specifically related to the sense organs
and the absorption of their respective sensations into consciousness.
The introduction by Ananda Shaktipada reads as follows.
After having revealed the unobstructed permanent absorption,
which is realized without any cause in the perspective of the rise of the twelve currents,
now the yoginis will explain the oral tradition of the five modes of activity, Charya.
By the emergence of five modes of activity, a state of waveless absorption is attained.
Commentary.
The five modes of activity are of the nature of
Anashrita, without support.
Abatuta, having thrown off all restrictions.
Unmata, mad, insane.
Savapaksha, all-consuming, and the great omnipervasive one, Mahaviyapaka.
Their emergence is a joyful upsurge of the nature of expansion,
which rises from within the collective energies, with or without restraint.
When this happens, nothing but the truth of unsurpassed absorption is experienced,
which is characterized as a complete pervasion, devoid of the fluctuations which arise in the case of the individual way,
the way of energy, and the divine way.
Anava, shakta, shambhava.
Now, this is surprising that even shambhava is excluded from this state because there is a fluctuation.
Any upaya has a movement, even shambhava.
Only an upaya is beyond.
Come back.
Now, I will explain in due order the five modes of activity in detail.
Anashrita.
In that context, the supportless mode, which is due to a state devoid of foundation,
arises in order to withdraw the objects of its own perception into consciousness,
by making sounds enter into the cavity of the ear.
It is of the nature of supreme space.
Our dhuta, the mode of having shaken off all conditionings,
is manifested by an unrestricted state on the part of the power of vision,
moving everywhere, in order to withdraw its own objects into consciousness.
Ummata, the mode of madness, related to the organ of smell,
is manifested freely like the behavior of a mindless lunatic,
who does not discriminate at the relationship between what is acceptable and what is not acceptable,
in order to absorb its respective objects into consciousness.
Sava Bhakshya, the all-consuming mode, related to the sense of taste,
has a tendency of swallowing all the residual traces, samskara, which are to be consumed.
It rises in order to devour its own objects, which are to be absorbed in consciousness.
At Sava Vyapika, the all-pervasive mode, is manifested by the activity of the sense of touch,
due to its only pervasiveness, in order to appropriate all the sensations of touch in consciousness.
This is the emergence of the Five Moods of Supreme Activity.
End of the quote of Ananda Shakti Bhada.
The interpretation by Swami Lakshman Chu differs from Ananda Shakti Bhada,
but it is too brief in what has come down to us,
because this is a transcript from an oral teaching, to be directly related to the Sutta.
However, as always, Swamiji provides the key for understanding the whole process.
He distinguishes charia from karma, action of the limited, individual way.
He defines it in the present context, which is in agreement with Ananda Shakti Bhada.
Quote,
When we enter through all the senses in God consciousness, then that act is called charia.
One version of his translation reads,
When observance of the five great acts gets established in the realized being,
the supreme state, where there is no agitation at all, is entered into.
And he describes the five acts as follows.
One, silence.
Two, agitative movement.
Three, agitated state.
Four, confirmation.
And five, supreme silence.
Known also as Niranjanatham.
The main difference between the two interpretations is that Swamiji takes the five modes of charia in the sense of stages of ascent.
Quote,
We have to start from objectivity in silenced mind.
Then agitative movement comes in our view in silence.
And that too we have got to be aware.
That awareness will lead us to the kingdom of God consciousness.
Confirmation of the agitated state is in no way other than the supreme spirit.
Now we understand what he means by agitation.
Not the ordinary Kshoba.
We also say it's not Kshoba.
But it is Spanda.
So, because we know that consciousness in this tradition is dynamic.
So it is not totally static.
But there is Spanda.
There is a dynamism of consciousness.
The supreme vibrative movement.
In that supreme behavior, there is no agitation at all.
In conclusion, I will come back to the five ways of charia as given by Amantashaktipada in this characteristic original terminology.
These five which are states of ecstasy related to the divinized senses.
Which absorb and transform their objects into pure consciousness.
They show the great freedom of the liberated being.
A freedom which finds expression in a variety of ways which reach their ultimate repose in a complete absorption.
